metaDescription: Order custom coins for corporate awards, employee recognition, and promotional giveaways. High-quality, engraved, and affordable bulk pricing.
introHtml:
Custom coins are typically struck from brass, zinc alloy, or stainless steel, offering a solid feel and lasting durability. They come in various sizes (1.5 to 2 inches) and thicknesses, with options for antique silver, gold, or dual-tone finishes. The raised or recessed design is achieved through striking, which creates a permanent impression that won't wear off over time. For bulk orders, this makes custom coins a reliable choice for long-term use in recognition programs, employee awards, or promotional giveaways.

Marketing directors often use custom coins as branded giveaways at trade shows and corporate events, where their weight and finish convey a sense of quality. HR directors and safety managers find them effective for service awards, safety milestones, or onboarding kits. Business owners appreciate that custom coins can be fully personalized with logos, text, and even edge lettering, making them versatile for any occasion. With low minimum order quantities and competitive wholesale pricing, custom coins fit both small-batch appreciation gifts and large-scale promotional runs.
buyingGuideHtml:
When ordering custom coins, start by choosing the right material and finish. Brass and zinc alloy are the most common, offering a premium feel at a reasonable cost. Stainless steel is more durable but heavier. Finishes like antique silver, gold, or dual-tone affect the final look and can match your brand colors. For a polished appearance, consider a soft enamel fill in the recessed areas, which adds color contrast and makes your logo stand out.

Decoration options include die-struck designs (raised or recessed), which are permanent and ideal for logos or text. For added detail, you can combine striking with color filling using epoxy or enamel. Edge lettering is another customization that works well for mottos or dates. Screen printing is not typical for coins because it wears off; stick to struck or engraved methods for longevity.

Common use cases for custom coins include employee recognition (years of service, safety awards), corporate gifts (customer appreciation, holiday tokens), and promotional giveaways at trade shows. They also work well for fundraising events, where donors receive a commemorative coin. Business owners often order them as unique business cards or membership tokens.

Quantity guidance: Most suppliers have a minimum order of 100 to 250 pieces for custom coins. As quantities increase, unit price drops significantly. For example, ordering 500 coins might cost $2–$3 each, while 2,000 pieces could be under $1.50 each. Plan your budget accordingly and consider ordering extras for future events, as reorders may have higher per-unit costs.

Avoid common mistakes: Don't choose a finish that hides your logo detail. Light-colored logos on antique silver can be hard to read. Also, ensure your artwork is vector-based (AI or EPS) for clean striking. Check the coin size: a 1.5-inch coin is good for a lapel pin, but a 2-inch coin is better for a challenge coin. Finally, confirm lead times—custom coins typically take 2–4 weeks for production, so plan ahead for event dates.

faqs.q: What are the minimum order quantities for custom coins?
faqs.a: Minimum order quantities typically start at 100 to 250 pieces, depending on the supplier and complexity of the design. Some may offer lower minimums for simple designs or higher minimums for dual-tone finishes.

faqs.q: What decoration methods are available for custom coins?
faqs.a: Common methods include die-struck (raised or recessed), soft enamel fill, and epoxy coating. For text or fine details, die-striking is best. Color fills add contrast but may wear over time. Edge lettering is also available.

faqs.q: How long does production take for custom coins?
faqs.a: Production typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from artwork approval. Rush orders may be available for an additional fee. Always confirm lead times with your supplier before placing an order.

faqs.q: Can I get a sample before placing a bulk order?
faqs.a: Yes, many suppliers offer sample coins for a fee, which is often credited toward your bulk order. Samples let you verify the finish, size, and detail quality before committing to a large run.

faqs.q: What materials are custom coins made from?
faqs.a: Custom coins are typically made from brass, zinc alloy, or stainless steel. Brass and zinc alloy are most common for their affordability and workability. Stainless steel is more durable but heavier and more expensive.

heroAltText: Custom coins with engraved logo and antique gold finish, ideal for corporate awards and promotional giveaways.
